rows.note: Published on the same grid and water balance as precipitation and potential evapotranspiration, so the three can be differenced without crossing models.

rows.label: Potential evapotranspiration
rows.note: Paired with actual evapotranspiration from one model, which is what makes their ratio a moisture index rather than a comparison of two conventions.

rows.label: Precipitation
rows.note: Downscaled to about four kilometres, which matters where a level-12 basin sits in mountain terrain and a coarse cell would average a valley with a ridge.

rows.label: Runoff
rows.note: TerraClimate publishes no runoff. This is a land-surface flux and is not discharge: it has not been routed and no gauge has been compared to it.

rows.label: Snow cover
rows.note: Its gaps grow towards the present at constant source coverage, so the series is published for inspection and withdrawn from trend analysis.

rows.label: Soil moisture
rows.note: A modelled column store in millimetres. It is published as what it is and not relabelled as the percentage the atlas attribute holds.

rows.label: Minimum temperature
rows.note: The month's daily minima, paired with the maxima from the same model.

rows.label: Mean temperature
rows.note: A true mean of hourly values. TerraClimate publishes only the daily extremes, and their midpoint is a different measurement that happens to carry the same name.

rows.label: Maximum temperature
rows.note: The month's daily maxima. ERA5-Land publishes no daily extreme on this grid.

rows.label: Unified Amu and Syr river-reach routing
rows.collection: Unified Amu and Syr river-reach routing
rows.note: Native HydroRIVERS HYRIV_ID to NEXT_DOWN routing across the complete Amu Darya and Syr Darya systems. The selection is not clipped at a national border and every nonzero target is present in the same table.

rows.label: Unified river reach to level-12 basin
rows.collection: Unified river reach to level-12 basin
rows.note: Native HydroRIVERS HYBAS_L12 association for every reach in the complete two-system frame. All referenced basin identities are present in the transboundary level-12 basin layer.

rows.label: River reach downstream routing
rows.note: Native HydroRIVERS NEXT_DOWN, restricted to reaches inside the selection. target_scope separates a reach that routes to another selected reach from an outlet and from one whose target lies outside Uzbekistan.

rows.label: River reach to level-12 basin
rows.note: The join that makes basins the reference frame. basin_scope records a reach whose basin is outside the published reference rather than dropping the row, which is how 3,073 orphaned reaches went unnoticed before.

rows.label: Water body to level-12 basin
rows.note: Resolved from the lake's pour point, falling back to its centroid. Spatial containment, not a native field of HydroLAKES.

rows.label: Basin downstream routing, levels 01-12
rows.note: Native HydroBASINS routing for every level of the extraction, with the scope of each target recorded against the selection.

rows.label: Basin nesting across levels
rows.note: Child to parent at adjacent levels, matched by Pfafstetter prefix and confirmed by spatial overlap. Every child resolves to exactly one parent.

rows.label: Pfafstetter code nesting
rows.note: The same nesting expressed in Pfafstetter codes rather than basin identifiers. Kept separate because the identifier scheme differs, so the two tables are not directly joinable.

rows.label: Measure
rows.collection: Environmental atlas layers by level-12 basin
rows.note: A measured overlay of every atlas package that has published vector geometry onto the basin reference, with overlap area for polygons, length for lines and a feature count for points. This is what lets a basin id reach the atlas: before it, the 134 packages were pinned to the country and nothing finer. Raster packages with only a PNG preview are absent until PIPELINES/raster_to_geojson.py gives them geometry; the manifest names them.

rows.label: Mean
rows.collection: Atlas raster surfaces read per level-12 basin
rows.note: Zonal statistics for every atlas package whose raster is georeferenced and carries a single data band: pixels, mean, min, max, stddev, and majority where the surface is categorical. Read value_kind first — mean describes a continuous surface, majority a classified one, and the mean of class codes means nothing. The rasters live inside an ESRI File Geodatabase within each 7-zip layer package, which is why the TIFF-only converter never found them. Seven packages are excluded and the manifest gives the reason for each: six are rendered RGB images or carry no georeference, and one is not on disk.

rows.label: Basin downstream routing, lake format, levels 01-12

rows.label: Shared km2
rows.note: Level-12 basins against the 14 first-level units — provinces, the autonomous republic and Tashkent city. Each row carries the area the two share, so a traced catchment can be attributed to the provinces that feed it. Every unit resolves to a place concept in the ontology, matched by P-code because the COD spellings differ from the vocabulary's. Carries no quality column because every row is a measured geometric overlap rather than a sensor reading — there is no sentinel or scaling fault for it to record.

rows.label: Shared km2
rows.note: The same overlay at the second level, across 199 districts, independent cities and gorhokimiyat towns. This is the resolution at which water administration actually happens, and the reason the districts carry no place concept: they are features, and the schema puts features in a table. Carries no quality column because every row is a measured geometric overlap rather than a sensor reading — there is no sentinel or scaling fault for it to record.

rows.label: Km2

rows.label: Km2

rows.note: Area of each land-cover class inside each canonical standard-format BasinATLAS level-12 catchment, once per year. rows.label: Precipitation total
rows.note: Accumulated rainfall per level-12 basin per pentad — days 1-5, 6-10, 11-15, 16-20, 21-25 and 26 to month end. CHIRPS is computed pentadally and its daily series is a disaggregation: summed over a month the two agree to within 0.00%, so the daily product adds nothing and its within-pentad variation is an artefact rather than an observation. Six pentads reconstruct a month to 0.0002 mm, which is why no monthly table is stored beside this one. The days column varies because the sixth pentad runs to month end, so an mm/day rate must divide by it rather than by five. Read at level 12 rather than level 7: at this product's 5.6 km grid a level-12 basin covers about four pixels, so it carries a value of its own, and the reduction costs no more because it is priced by the raster read rather than the polygon count. CFSv2 stays at level 7 because its 34.8 km grid puts nine and a half level-12 basins inside one pixel.

rows.label: Ghm mean
rows.note: Cumulative human modification for 2016 — settlement, agriculture, transport, mining and energy, electrical infrastructure — as a 0 to 1 index at 1 km, from thirteen source datasets. The basin rows use the canonical standard BasinATLAS level-12 identifier frame. Stored with the area share in each modification band beside the mean, because a mean of 0.3 describes both a uniformly semi-modified landscape and a city beside a desert. Carries no quality column: every row is a measured geometric reduction of a single complete image. The layer is timeless in the strict sense — the collection holds one image with no system:time_start — so there is nothing to refresh and no period it can fall behind. Measured over both frames because human modification belongs to whoever governs a place as much as to whatever drains it, and the frame changes the answer: over basins Uzbekistan averages 0.33, over districts 0.61, because districts are drawn around settlement while basins include the empty desert between it.
